items.title: Anthropic argues for reading models through their own neurons
items.what_happened: Two Anthropic alignment posts argue that plain neurons are more readable than people assume. Without training, neuron probes beat text search on 11 of 16 safety sets and helped a blind auditor name hidden behaviours in 75% of cases, against 40% from outputs alone.
items.why_it_matters: It questions the default move to sparse autoencoders for safety work. It also finds that many WMDP unlearning methods seem to hide knowledge rather than remove it.
items.what_to_watch: Whether others reproduce the results on larger models and longer finetunes. Also watch for a code release, since none is mentioned.
items.uncertainty: Model organisms were mostly short finetunes. On one security news set, label-free probes did no better than chance.

items.title: METR updates its time-horizon method and says capabilities are getting harder to measure
items.what_happened: METR released a new task suite, TH2, with 36 tasks split into verifiable and judgment-heavy subsets. It estimates that time horizons double about every 3.6 months, and up to about 27 hours on verifiable tasks.
items.why_it_matters: Models do well on tasks with fast feedback but worse on judgment tasks. AI judges also rated outputs from similar or stronger models too highly, a direct warning for LLM-as-judge evaluation.
items.what_to_watch: Critiques of the new estimates, since human baselines inform only 9% of task time estimates. Also watch whether others adopt the new METR Capability Index.
items.uncertainty: The authors say most time estimates come from researchers, not measured baselines. The acceleration findings depend on method choices.

items.title: Debate over OpenAI's idea of perplexity as a shared safety limit
items.what_happened: OpenAI's chief scientist reportedly posted an essay on 22 November sharing an internal pretraining perplexity curve. It proposes perplexity-linked limits shared by all frontier labs. Critics said the number depends on the tokenizer, evaluation method and a private test set.
items.why_it_matters: It is a concrete proposal to tie safety rules to one measurable training signal. The critique shows why such a metric is hard to compare across labs and misses gains from reasoning and RL.
items.what_to_watch: Whether labs agree on a neutral test set or on bits per byte. Also watch whether other labs publish comparable numbers.

source.name: DEV Community analysis of the OpenAI post

items.uncertainty: The original OpenAI page could not be opened. Its content comes from secondary reports that agree with each other.

notes: Covered the Anthropic alignment blog, transformer-circuits.pub, DeepMind, OpenAI alignment, ICLR and NeurIPS pages, the Alignment Forum and METR. The original OpenAI perplexity post could not be opened. The Meta FAIR blog was blocked.
